project.name: quantzhai
project.description: A local Codex stack for running Qwen through a turboquant llama.cpp server with an OpenAI-compatible proxy that bridges Codex CLI to a local llama.cpp backend.

nodes.name: GEMINI.md
nodes.summary: Agent behaviour guide for the QuantZhai project covering development rules, git workflow, debugging doctrine, telemetry conventions, BrainCase memory constraints, and proxy policy authority. Mirrors CLAUDE.md and serves as the Gemini-targeted equivalent.

nodes.name: quantzhai_proxy.py
nodes.summary: Main proxy server entry point implementing an OpenAI-compatible HTTP handler (ProxyHandler) that bridges Codex CLI Responses API calls to a local llama.cpp backend, handling SSE streaming, telemetry emission, rate-limit headers, compaction, and model routing.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Python's built-in http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler for the HTTP layer; all proxy logic is class-level state on ProxyHandler with class-level singleton modules injected at startup.

nodes.name: ProxyHandler
nodes.summary: HTTP request handler bridging Codex CLI to the local llama.cpp backend; dispatches GET/POST to Ollama-compatible, Responses API, and telemetry SSE endpoints, and performs SSE stream transformation with telemetry injection.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Initialises all proxy subsystems (model catalog, router, backend, telemetry, request tracker, recovery jobs, braincase tools), configures the HTTP server with optional TLS, and runs the serve loop.

nodes.name: qz_active_requests.py
nodes.summary: Provides a thread-safe counter and snapshot tracker for in-flight proxy requests, used by the control plane and recovery subsystems to gate admission and monitor concurrency.

nodes.name: ActiveRequestTracker
nodes.summary: Thread-safe counter tracking in-flight HTTP requests with begin/finish lifecycle methods and a snapshot view for monitoring.

nodes.name: qz_backend_manager.py
nodes.summary: Manages the lifecycle of the llama.cpp backend process (or Docker container), including start/stop/restart, GPU offload detection, autostart-with-delay, health checking, and Docker command construction.

nodes.name: BackendManager
nodes.summary: Manages start, stop, restart, and health monitoring of the llama.cpp backend process; builds Docker or native launch arguments and emits telemetry events on state transitions.

nodes.name: BackendState
nodes.summary: Data container representing a backend process snapshot, including phase, PID, launch timestamps, model slug, and serialisation to dict.

nodes.name: qz_backend.py
nodes.summary: HTTP client for the llama.cpp backend API supporting model load/unload, health polling, JSON GET/POST helpers, Docker container control, and synchronous wait-for-ready polling.

nodes.name: BackendClient
nodes.summary: HTTP client for the llama.cpp server exposing model load, unload, health check, model listing, and Docker container management operations.

nodes.name: qz_braincase_db.py
nodes.summary: Low-level SQLite storage layer for the BrainCase memory system, providing schema initialisation, CRUD operations for state records and source refs, full-text search via FTS5, and FTS index management.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses SQLite FTS5 for full-text search with a fallback to exact/tag search when FTS is unavailable; schema versioning via SQLite user_version pragma.

nodes.name: BrainCaseDB
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed storage engine for BrainCase memory records: manages state record lifecycle (put, get, list, promote, retire, supersede), source ref provenance, FTS5 full-text search, and schema migrations.

nodes.name: qz_braincase_render.py
nodes.summary: Renders BrainCase memory records into compact text packets for injection into LLM context, with budget-aware packing, eligibility filtering, and structured render-packet envelopes.

nodes.name: render_pack
nodes.summary: Packs eligible BrainCase records into a character-budget-limited render blob, ordering by tier priority and truncating to fit the context window.

nodes.name: braincase_render_packet
nodes.summary: Assembles the full render packet dict that wraps the packed memory lines with metadata for injection into a tool result.

nodes.name: qz_braincase_retention.py
nodes.summary: Implements retention policy evaluation for BrainCase records, including duration parsing, rule matching, and per-record retention decisions covering expiry, archival, and deletion.

nodes.name: retention_decision_for_record
nodes.summary: Evaluates all retention rules against a state record and returns the final retention decision (keep, archive, delete) with the matching rule details.

nodes.name: qz_braincase_review.py
nodes.summary: Provides operator-facing review operations for BrainCase candidate records: listing, inspection, promotion, rejection, retention reporting, and pruning.

nodes.name: promote_candidate_record
nodes.summary: Promotes a candidate BrainCase record to active status after running dedup, conflict, and retention checks.

nodes.name: apply_retention_prune
nodes.summary: Applies retention policy decisions across all eligible BrainCase records, retiring or deleting records that have exceeded their configured retention window.

nodes.name: qz_braincase_tools.py
nodes.summary: Implements the BrainCase tool-plane: tool definitions, executor classes, render/recall/write-candidate tool handlers, and harness-injection logic for appending BrainCase tools to outgoing Codex request bodies.

nodes.name: braincase_recall_packet
nodes.summary: Executes a BrainCase recall query across configured memory tiers and assembles the result packet for the model.

nodes.name: braincase_write_candidate_tool
nodes.summary: Handles the write-candidate tool call: validates arguments, resolves scope, runs dedup/conflict checks, and writes or updates a candidate state record via braincase_write.

nodes.name: inject_braincase_tools_to_body
nodes.summary: Injects BrainCase tool definitions into an outgoing request body if BrainCase tools are enabled and the request lacks existing tool definitions.

nodes.name: _BraincaseBaseExecutor
nodes.summary: Base class for BrainCase proxy tool executors, providing DB access, argument parsing, call-ID matching, and result packaging.

nodes.name: qz_braincase_write.py
nodes.summary: Implements the write path for BrainCase state records: scope resolution, dedup checking, conflict detection, source linking, and the actual write and update operations against BrainCaseDB.

nodes.name: braincase_write_state_record
nodes.summary: Writes a new BrainCase state record to the DB after running scope resolution, dedup, and conflict checks.

nodes.name: braincase_update_state_record
nodes.summary: Updates an existing BrainCase state record, re-running conflict and dedup checks and superseding the prior record.

nodes.name: qz_codex_catalog.py
nodes.summary: Generates the Codex-visible model catalog JSON from the proxy's model catalog and prompt policy, translating internal profiles into the Codex-compatible model manifest format.

nodes.name: build_live_model
nodes.summary: Builds a single Codex model entry dict from a catalog profile, applying overrides for context length, reasoning level, and other Codex-visible fields.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Generates the full Codex model catalog manifest by iterating all catalog profiles and writing the output JSON file.

nodes.name: qz_codex_client_config.py
nodes.summary: Generates the Codex client configuration payload (base URL, catalog path, freshness metadata) served to Codex on startup.

nodes.name: qz_codex_metadata.py
nodes.summary: Extracts and normalises request metadata from Codex HTTP headers and request bodies, including session/window identity, workspace resolution, turn metadata, memory domain config, and full request context assembly.

nodes.name: extract_codex_identity
nodes.summary: Extracts a structured CodexIdentity from HTTP headers, resolving session, window, workspace, and remote URL fields.

nodes.name: extract_codex_request_context
nodes.summary: Assembles a complete CodexRequestContext by combining identity, turn metadata, body metadata, and memory domain resolution into a single context object.

nodes.name: qz_config_report.py
nodes.summary: Produces a comprehensive effective configuration report for the proxy, covering prompt files, model overrides, memory domain config, search policy, and operational store health.

nodes.name: effective_config_payload
nodes.summary: Assembles the full effective configuration report dict including prompt stack, model overrides, memory domains, search policy, and operational store status.

nodes.name: qz_control_plane.py
nodes.summary: Builds the proxy control-plane status payload aggregating backend state, model status, recovery state, active requests, VRAM snapshot, and model catalog into a unified /qz/status response.

nodes.name: build_control_plane_status
nodes.summary: Aggregates backend manager, model status, recovery, VRAM, and catalog information into the full /qz/status JSON payload.

nodes.name: qz_feedback.py
nodes.summary: Defines feedback visibility, channel, and signal-decision enums used to classify and render advisory messages and coercion errors back to the Codex client.

nodes.name: qz_file_signal.py
nodes.summary: Detects repeated file-read patterns in tool call sequences and emits advisory signals when the same file is read multiple times without intervening writes, helping identify stuck loops.

nodes.name: repeated_read_signal
nodes.summary: Evaluates accumulated tool call history against a repeated-read state and returns a RepeatedReadDecision indicating whether an advisory should be emitted.

nodes.name: qz_model_catalog.py
nodes.summary: Core model catalog: scans the var/models directory for GGUF symlinks, reads GGUF metadata headers, applies manifest/override layering, and exposes a ModelCatalog class for profile resolution, selection, and serialisation.
nodes.languageNotes: Parses GGUF binary file headers directly in Python to extract model name, architecture, and context length without external dependencies.

nodes.name: ModelCatalog
nodes.summary: Central model catalog object managing profile scanning, refresh, selection, resolution, and serialisation to Codex/Ollama API formats.

nodes.name: build_entry
nodes.summary: Builds a fully-merged catalog entry for a model profile by combining GGUF metadata, manifest declarations, and runtime overrides.

nodes.name: scan_models
nodes.summary: Scans the model inventory directory for valid GGUF symlinks and returns a list of discovered profile paths.

nodes.name: qz_model_load_failure.py
nodes.summary: Classifies model load failures from backend log output into structured failure categories (OOM, timeout, corrupt file, etc.) for telemetry and error reporting.

nodes.name: qz_model_router.py
nodes.summary: Central model routing layer: the ModelRouter class manages model selection, context length determination, backend model state reconciliation, load/unload orchestration, status snapshots, and Ollama-compatible API handler delegation.

nodes.name: ModelRouter
nodes.summary: Orchestrates model selection, context length resolution, backend model loading/unloading, runtime state persistence, and status reporting for the proxy.

nodes.name: qz_model_state.py
nodes.summary: Persists and loads the model selection state (selected profile, context length, load success/failure timestamps) to/from a JSON file on disk, providing durable model state across proxy restarts.

nodes.name: ModelState
nodes.summary: Data container for persisted model selection state, including profile identity, context length, and load success/failure history.

nodes.name: qz_model_status.py
nodes.summary: Derives and formats the model status block for the control plane, combining backend loaded-model state, backend manager phase, model selection state, and admission gating into a unified status payload with recommended recovery actions.

nodes.name: build_model_status
nodes.summary: Assembles the full model status dict from backend, manager, and selection state, computing admission state and recommended recovery actions.

nodes.name: qz_native_tool_output.py
nodes.summary: Classifies native Codex tool outputs by exit code and content, producing structured signal decisions and feedback for advisory rendering.

nodes.name: qz_operational_store.py
nodes.summary: SQLite-backed operational event and runtime-fact store for the proxy, recording startup events, runtime key-value facts, and providing a recent-events query for the config report.

nodes.name: OperationalStore
nodes.summary: SQLite store for operational events and key-value runtime facts, with schema initialisation, safe-execute error handling, and a recent-events query.

nodes.name: qz_paths.py
nodes.summary: Central path resolver for the QuantZhai project, providing functions to locate the project root, var directory, model inventory, and Codex-generated config files.

nodes.name: qz_prompt_policy.py
nodes.summary: Assembles the instruction stack sent to the LLM by loading base prompts, model overrides, turn harness definitions, and proxy-added instruction blocks according to manifest-driven prompt policy.

nodes.name: assemble_instruction_stack
nodes.summary: Builds the final ordered instruction list for an LLM request by merging base prompt blocks, profile overrides, and proxy-injected instruction blocks.

nodes.name: qz_proxy_config.py
nodes.summary: Defines proxy API contract constants and helper data structures, including endpoint path constants and the api_contract_payload factory used to advertise supported API surface to Codex.

nodes.name: qz_proxy_tools.py
nodes.summary: Implements the proxy-local tool registry and execution framework, providing ProxyLocalToolRegistry and associated executor classes that intercept, coerce, and execute tool calls (web search, braincase) before upstream or on behalf of Codex.

nodes.name: ProxyLocalToolRegistry
nodes.summary: Central registry that routes and executes proxy-local tool calls, managing lifecycle events, continuation logic, and telemetry for all intercepted tools including web search and braincase.

nodes.name: WebSearchProxyToolExecutor
nodes.summary: Proxy-local executor for web search tool calls, coercing arguments and dispatching to the WebSearchRuntime.

nodes.name: ProxyLocalToolExecutor
nodes.summary: Abstract base for proxy-local tool executors defining the is_call, started_public_item, and execute interface.

nodes.name: make_proxy_local_tool_registry
nodes.summary: Factory function that assembles a ProxyLocalToolRegistry from web_runtime and braincase db dependencies.

nodes.name: qz_reasoning_policy.py
nodes.summary: Defines the reasoning policy layer for Qwen, mapping reasoning level strings (low/medium/high) to sampling parameters and thinking token budgets, and applying them to outgoing request bodies.

nodes.name: apply_reasoning_policy
nodes.summary: Applies the resolved reasoning policy to a request body, setting sampling parameters and the thinking budget prefix.

nodes.name: qz_recovery_jobs.py
nodes.summary: Provides RecoveryJobStore, a thread-safe bounded in-memory store for tracking recovery job lifecycle states (pending, running, completed, failed) with timestamps.

nodes.name: RecoveryJobStore
nodes.summary: Thread-safe bounded store for recovery job records supporting create, mark_running, mark_completed, mark_failed, and snapshot operations.

nodes.name: qz_recovery_plan.py
nodes.summary: Implements the recovery plan builder that analyses current service status and operator action to produce an actionable plan dict with flags for catalog refresh, model selection, backend start/restart, and failure clearing.

nodes.name: build_recovery_plan
nodes.summary: Evaluates service status, active requests, backoff state, and operator-requested action to produce a complete recovery plan dict with step flags and human-readable notes.

nodes.name: qz_recovery_state.py
nodes.summary: Defines RecoveryRuntimeState, which tracks per-action attempt counts, exponential backoff schedules, and manual hold flags for the backend recovery system.

nodes.name: RecoveryRuntimeState
nodes.summary: Thread-safe runtime state manager for backend recovery tracking attempt counters, backoff windows, manual hold flags, and last-error records per recovery action.

nodes.name: qz_recovery_status.py
nodes.summary: Builds the recovery status payload from service status, runtime state, active requests, and job store for use in the /qz/status and recovery API responses.

nodes.name: build_recovery_status
nodes.summary: Assembles a structured recovery status dict from service_status, runtime_state, active_requests, and recovery_jobs, mapping action codes to human labels.

nodes.name: qz_request_normalization.py

nodes.name: normalize_responses_input_for_qwen
nodes.summary: Top-level normalization entry point that cleans input items, applies tool history replay filtering, strips/injects turn harnesses, and injects braincase tools into the request body.

nodes.name: clean_content
nodes.summary: Strips reasoning think-tags, redundant numbered starts, and stale output markers from text content to reduce context noise for the model.

nodes.name: _canonicalize_message
nodes.summary: Converts a Responses API message item into a normalized flat text representation, handling multi-part content blocks, function outputs, and refusals.

nodes.name: qz_request_router.py
nodes.summary: Core HTTP request router that handles all proxy endpoints including Responses API streaming and JSON calls, model management, recovery triggering, Codex catalog refresh, VRAM status, and telemetry; the central orchestration layer of the proxy.
nodes.languageNotes: RequestRouter is a 3000+ line mega-class handling the full proxy surface; consider the recovery, model, and streaming sections as distinct sub-concerns.

nodes.name: RequestRouter
nodes.summary: Main orchestration class implementing handle_get and handle_post routing for all proxy endpoints, including Responses API, recovery, model select/reload, VRAM snapshots, and Codex catalog management.

nodes.name: qz_responses_error.py
nodes.summary: Provides error payload builders for the OpenAI Responses API, normalizing error codes, detecting deprecated aliases, and constructing standards-compliant error response dicts.

nodes.name: build_responses_error_payload
nodes.summary: Constructs a complete Responses API error payload dict from error code, message, and optional metadata, handling normalization and nested error structure.

nodes.name: qz_responses_stream.py
nodes.summary: Implements ResponsesStreamRuntime, the central SSE streaming engine that reads upstream llama.cpp streams, transforms events, manages hop state, executes proxy-local tools, handles timeouts/watchdog, and delivers correctly-formed Codex-visible SSE output.

nodes.name: ResponsesStreamRuntime

nodes.name: StreamHopState

nodes.name: StreamRunState

nodes.name: qz_responses.py

nodes.name: qz_runtime_io.py
nodes.summary: Provides capture I/O helpers for writing request/response payloads to var/captures/, managing capture modes (off/latest/full/request-scoped), and reading runtime state files.

nodes.name: CapturePolicy

nodes.name: qz_search_config.py

nodes.name: SearchConfigResult

nodes.name: load_search_config

nodes.name: qz_search_policy.py

nodes.name: qz_service_status.py

nodes.name: build_service_status

nodes.name: make_response_stream_events

nodes.name: qz_stream_terminal.py

nodes.name: qz_telemetry.py

tour.title: Start Here: Agent Rules & Architecture Overview
tour.description: GEMINI.md is the agent behaviour guide that explains the entire project's development rules, debugging doctrine, BrainCase constraints, and proxy policy authority. Read this first to understand the mental model: the proxy is the single source of truth, runtime state lives in var/, and agents must follow evidence-first debugging. It mirrors CLAUDE.md and tells you what every subsystem owns.

tour.title: The Proxy Entry Point
tour.description: quantzhai_proxy.py is where it all begins. It implements ProxyHandler (a Python BaseHTTPRequestHandler subclass) and the main() function that starts the HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:18180. On startup it wires together the model catalog, backend manager, model router, telemetry bus, search config, and recovery state — all the singletons that live for the lifetime of the process. Every Codex request arrives here first.

tour.title: HTTP Request Routing: The Central Orchestrator
tour.description: qz_request_router.py (3,363 lines, fan-out 30) is the central orchestration hub. RequestRouter dispatches every HTTP path: /v1/responses for Codex requests, /qz/status for control-plane reads, /qz/recover for operator-triggered recovery, /v1/models for catalog, and a dozen more. It validates headers, gates admission, triggers streaming or JSON paths, and coordinates recovery actions. Understanding this file reveals the full API surface of the proxy.

tour.title: Request Normalization: Translating Codex → Qwen
tour.description: Before any request reaches llama.cpp, qz_request_normalization.py transforms it: stripping think-tags from prior turns, injecting turn harnesses, canonicalizing message format, cleaning content, and injecting BrainCase tools into the tool list. qz_codex_metadata.py extracts the session identity, workspace, memory domain config, and full request context from Codex headers. Together these two files define the Codex→Qwen translation layer.

tour.title: SSE Streaming Engine
tour.description: qz_responses_stream.py (2,433 lines) implements ResponsesStreamRuntime — the heart of the proxy. It reads raw llama.cpp SSE chunks, calls qz_sse.py to transform them into OpenAI Responses API events, manages multi-hop tool execution state, fires proxy-local tools (web search, braincase), handles watchdog timeouts via qz_stream_watchdog.py, and classifies terminal events via qz_stream_terminal.py. Most proxy bugs live in this file.

tour.title: Tool Execution Framework
tour.description: The tool layer intercepts Codex tool calls before forwarding upstream. qz_tools.py defines the base types (ToolLifecycleSpec, ToolAdapter, ToolRegistry). qz_proxy_tools.py holds ProxyLocalToolRegistry, which decides whether each tool call should be executed locally or forwarded. qz_tool_lifecycle.py tracks tool call state across streaming hops. qz_tool_request.py normalises tool schemas for llama.cpp's function_call format. qz_tool_apply_patch.py handles the critical apply_patch adapter.

tour.title: Web Search Tool
tour.description: qz_tool_web.py (2,326 lines) implements WebSearchRuntime and WebSearchToolAdapter — the full SearXNG-backed web search engine. It handles search querying, page fetching and content extraction, source trust scoring, result formatting, provider guidance injection, strict profile enforcement, and budget management. The search config (qz_search_config.py) and search policy (qz_search_policy.py) control which provider profile is active.

tour.title: Model Management Layer
tour.description: qz_model_catalog.py scans var/models/ for GGUF symlinks, reads GGUF metadata headers, and applies manifest/override layering to build the profile registry. qz_model_router.py (ModelRouter, 1,418 lines) selects the active profile, determines context length, reconciles loaded backend state, and orchestrates model load/unload. qz_model_state.py persists the selection to disk so it survives proxy restarts. qz_reasoning_policy.py maps reasoning level strings to Qwen sampling params.

tour.title: Backend Infrastructure: llama.cpp Lifecycle
tour.description: qz_backend.py is the HTTP client for the llama.cpp API — it handles model load/unload requests, health polling, and synchronous wait-for-ready. qz_backend_manager.py manages the OS-level process or Docker container lifecycle: start, stop, restart, GPU offload detection, autostart-with-delay. qz_vram_snapshot.py (1,742 lines) probes llama.cpp slots/props endpoints and nvidia-smi to build the VRAM telemetry snapshot with KV cache estimation.

tour.title: BrainCase Memory Subsystem
tour.description: BrainCase is the tool-mediated LLM memory layer. qz_braincase_db.py is the SQLite storage substrate (CRUD, FTS5 search). qz_braincase_tools.py is the tool-plane entry point — it defines the braincase_render, braincase_recall, and braincase_write_candidate tools and injects them into outgoing request bodies. qz_braincase_render.py packs records into LLM-context-sized packets. qz_braincase_write.py handles scope resolution and dedup on the write path. Remember: BrainCaseDB is storage only, never automatic ingestion.

tour.title: Control Plane, Telemetry & Recovery
tour.description: qz_control_plane.py assembles the /qz/status payload from all subsystems. qz_service_status.py builds the comprehensive service status dict. The recovery subsystem (qz_recovery_state.py, qz_recovery_plan.py, qz_recovery_jobs.py, qz_recovery_status.py) implements exponential-backoff retry logic and operator-triggered recovery actions. qz_telemetry.py provides TelemetryBus, the thread-safe in-process event bus used by monitors and the qz-top dashboard.
